title: Narada asks the chant's rules
hookLine: every app wants you to accept its terms. a sage asks for the chant's terms
carry: the names of God need no rules
tomorrow: what happens when a whole room sings the names back?
last: A WORD CAN KEEP GOING AFTER THE VOICE STOPS.

lines: HARE, KRISHNA, RAMA, ON THE RADIO.
A SAGE ASKS A PRACTICAL QUESTION.
cards: Every new app wants you to accept its terms before it lets you in. Here's a chant that was asked for its terms, and the answer is the surprise.
George Harrison, the Beatles' lead guitarist, put out a love song to God, and partway through, the backing voices slide into Hindu names: Hare, Krishna, Rama.
A chant from a Sanskrit text was suddenly playing on the radio. It started with a sage asking a very practical question.

teach.h: HOW DO I CROSS THE HARD AGE?
teach.b: The text is the Kali-Santarana Upanishad, and it's short. The sage Narada goes to Brahma, the creator, worried about the age of Kali, the hard age to come. How do I cross it?
Brahma's answer: by the names of the Lord. Then he gives the chant itself, Rama half first: Hare Rama Hare Rama, Rama Rama Hare Hare, Hare Krishna Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna Hare Hare.
Narada, being thorough, asks for the rules.
And Brahma says there are none. No rule of time, place or purity for the names. Nothing in it waits for permission.

teach.h: A WEEK OF IDEAS ON THE ROAD.
teach.b: Now hold the week up to the light. Gandhi read a war poem as the war inside, and let go of the fruit. King kept his faith and took the method.
A hymn found the true devotee in someone who feels another's pain. A band went to Rishikesh for a quiet word.

teach.h: NO RULES OF TIME, PLACE OR PURITY.
teach.b: Patanjali said to mean it every time. Manu let it go silent, and Hannah's lips moved with no sound. And a chant with no terms at all ended up on the radio.

how: Devotees of Krishna and Rama chant the Hare Krishna mantra on beads in japa, and sing it together in kirtan, at home, in temples and in public.

games.q: your grandfather can't get to the temple anymore, and worries that his chanting from a hospital bed doesn't count. what does the Kali-Santarana say?
o: the names carry no rule of time, place or purity; they count right there.
they'll count once he's back at the temple and can finish them properly.
only someone at the temple can say them for him while he's away.
games.why: Narada asks for the chant's rules, and Brahma says there are none: no rule of time, place or purity for the names.

practice: If the names are yours, say them now, softly or only in the mind, right where you are, with no washing or setting up first: Hare Rama, Hare Krishna. If you don't pray, take one word you hold dear and do the same.
Let each name go by at the pace of a slow breath, and when the mind wanders, come back to the next one.
